citations.quote: This fall in 2015 sci Zone will be flight testing the QuickSAT/Xen Space Hypervisor and the prototype of the FRNCS-P Flight Computer as a hosted payload on the AFRL based SHARC Satellite. The SHARC Satellite is a 5U CubeSAT that will be deployed from the International Space Station via the NanoRacks Program.

QuickSAT $ ^{\mathrm{TM}} $ with the open source stepSATdb data architecture is a satellite design, mission planning, and product lifecycle management framework and environment. Key new features include in the QuickSAT environment include: assignment of virtual machines to processor cores, defining virtual machine parameters, mapping parameters between the satellite bus and the hypervisor, vehicle management and configuration control specific to the unique features of the space hypervisor, and Xen monitoring and control tools via an on board web interface.

The QuickSAT environment is an architecture that encapsulates the space vehicle development and utilization process from concept capture through flight management. Currently a host of tools is available from systems engineering and design, system testing, software definition, vehicle health and management and ground control.

QuickSAT/Designer was developed based on a need to detail the relationships between the satellite configuration (components, payloads and interrelationships), manage inventories, provide for life cycle management, design, analysis and test data, and to automate the design and manufacturing process.

step_SATdb seamlessly integrates existing detail design tools with QuickSAT, as well as databases tracking requirements, hardware and software components and parts in inventory, along with the final configuration of the satellite. QuickSAT provides for rapid design and coherency between a range of applications and data sets. step_SATdb stores and distributes supporting satellite design, configuration, mission, support and test data from a centralized database and can distribute the data across multiple platforms and via the internet and proprietary networks.

- Mission planning including mission phase, flight legs and modes of operation for each flight leg.

- Modes of operation can define which systems and payloads are in use for a given mode.
- Power modeling - both systems level and detail based on modes of flight for each flight leg.

- Integration with external tools including Matlab, Mathematica, SOAP and STK.

- Satellite test and health monitoring

With QuickSAT/Designer you can save multiple configurations of a given satellite model and flight plan and compare the models, design and analytics results. Designs are fully traceable and you can baseline a mission or alternative flight plans from prior projects. Payloads and their software can be modified, however prior versions are stored to maintain fully traceable models and designs. Payloads can be easily swapped out in QuickSAT.

Currently, several clouds are active, one of which, www.quick-sat.com, serves NASA, Leidos, government subcontractors and the University Nanosat Community, plus others who support satellite development.

As shown in Figure 4, the user will be able to define their mission, including satellite subsystems and payloads. Through QuickSAT, the user can then define the mission flight plan and modes of operation, defining which elements of the satellite are operational for each mode of flight, covering mass, power and volume. Using the flight plan and mode information, the user can define a schedule of which modes are operational based on conditions, or events, for a given flight leg through the QuickSAT/Scheduler. For example defining the conditions to turn on an imager, when to transmit data or when to go into a safe hold mode. Using this knowledge we can define an event driven schedule and model and simulate other factors such as power utilization throughout a mission or propellants used.

The goal of current research is to combine the security, robustness and performance of the Xen with ARINC 653 modules open source hypervisor with the proven QuickSAT/step_SATdb architecture to create the QuickSAT/Xen Space Hypervisor environment.
This schedule of conditions along with payload software models and applications are downloaded from QuickSAT to the vehicle on board processor and the Xen Space Hypervisor
The Xen Space Hypervisor will then create and operate the virtualized payloads, providing all the security, robustness and performance expected from an ARINC 653 based hypervisor.

Utilizing QuickSAT's flight planning tools along with its payload and satellite definition and modeling tools will allow for the creation Virtualized payloads which will increase the beneficial mission utility and life of space platforms while decreasing acquisition time and cost, as will be demonstrated throughout the SBIR effort.

To test and verify sci_Zone technologies, AFRL has invited sci_Zone to participate in the SHARC mission, a 5U cube sat to be launched via the Nanoracks deployer from the International Space Station. sci_Zone has been given 1.5U to host our payload, principally the FRNCS-P flight computer running QuickSAT/Xen $ ^{viii} $ and our flight management system QuickSAT/VMS (Vehicle Management System). In addition we will be testing our LinkStar radio which provides 24/7 radio communications between the payload and ground. The key objective of our mission is to demonstrate the functionality of a hypervisor computer system for space applications. Secondary objectives include: FRNCS-P, QuickSAT/VMS, and LinkStar space flight qualification.

The FRNCS-P flight computer is comprised of two separate computer boards, connected via both Ethernet and serial line links. The Host, running QuickSAT/Xen and the virtual machines/payloads (VM) uses the AllWinnerTech A20/ARM Cortex-A7 Dual Core chip with 16GB of RAM. Each VM will be running Ubuntu (14.04). The gateway computer runs the primary flight management system, QuickSAT/VMS, including providing command and control, backup storage and is the link to the LinkStar radio and the ground communications system. The gateway computer runs an ARM8 processor at 1Ghz, 4GB RAM and Debian Linux (7.6).

QuickSAT/VMS will operate on the FRNCS-P gateway, storing all data in the stepSATdb_Flight on board database. The QS/Communications Manager packages and sends the data to the LinkStar radio, where the information is moved through the GlobalStar Network via TCP/IP link.

The SHARC mission represents a remarkable opportunity to test, demonstrate and flight certify the entire QuickSAT architecture, the FRNCS-P flight computer QuickSAT will run on and the LinkStar radio providing 24/7 ground communications.
Santangelo, Andrew, "QuickSAT/step_SATdb: A Satellite Concurrent Design Automation and Design for Manufacturability cloud based environment for Responsive Space", AIAA-2426, September 28, 2011.
Santangelo, Andrew, "An Open Source Space Hypervisor For Small Satellites", AIAA 2013-5512, Space 2013 Conference, September 10-12, 2013, San Diego, California, 2013
QuickSAT/Xen Space Hypervisor, is a space qualified hypervisor, that will support the virtualization of satellite payloads, systems and software modules on a full range of satellites.
